riskUniverse.omittedRiskNote: The complete AIRUM risk universe contains more risks than shown here; this repository intentionally publishes only this reduced source-backed subset.

risks.name: AI Ambition-Feasibility Mismatch
risks.description: Pursuing disruptive AI ambitions without the requisite technology maturity, data readiness, or organizational buy-in, leading to project failure.
risks.expectedControlName: AI strategy feasibility and readiness review
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require each material AI ambition, roadmap item, or major use case to document business objective, feasibility assumptions, data/process readiness, capability gaps, funding, accountable owner, and decision gate before investment approval.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Confirm AI ambitions are achievable, resourced, and aligned to realistic organizational readiness before commitments are made.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Roadmap; Gartner: AI Strategy; ISO/IEC 42001 (Context of Org); NIST AI RMF: MAP 1.1, MAP 1.2). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Competitive Race Risk
risks.description: Rapidly deploying AI systems to maximize strategic advantage, prioritizing speed over safety or diligence (The "AI Race").
risks.expectedControlName: Responsible AI competition and escalation guardrail
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require leadership review of competitive-pressure decisions, including documented risk appetite, minimum control baseline, release criteria, and escalation where market pressure would bypass governance or validation.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Prevent speed-to-market pressure from overriding AI governance, validation, safety, privacy, or ethical safeguards.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (MIT AI Risk Rep: 6.4 (Competitive Dynamics); Gartner: Risk Essentials; NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 1.2, MAP 1.5). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Strategic Misalignment
risks.description: AI initiatives do not deliver on key strategic goals, fail to adapt to business priorities, or are disconnected from the broader business strategy.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Maintain a reviewed AI portfolio linking each material AI initiative to strategy, business process, value hypothesis, risk owner, and approved success measures.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure AI initiatives support defined business objectives and are governed as part of the enterprise portfolio.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Strategy; MITRE: Strategy & Resources; ISO/IEC 42001 (Leadership); NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 1.1, GOVERN 1.3). risks.name: Lack of Clear Accountability
risks.description: Roles for AI development, oversight, and "human-in-the-loop" decision rights are not clearly defined, leading to responsibility gaps.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Assign documented business, technical, risk, data, model, vendor, and control owners for each material AI system, including decision rights and escalation paths.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Make AI ownership, decision accountability, and control responsibility explicit and testable.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Organization; MITRE: Org Structure; ISO/IEC 42001 (Roles A.3.2); NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 2.1, GOVERN 2.3). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Missing AI Inventory
risks.description: Failure to maintain a complete, current inventory of AI systems, models, use cases, automations, and owners prevents risk classification, oversight, monitoring, and compliance.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Maintain a complete and periodically reconciled AI inventory capturing owner, purpose, process, data, vendor, classification, lifecycle stage, and control status for material AI use.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure AI use is visible, owned, classified, and available for risk management and audit scoping.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Governance (Inventory); ISO/IEC 5338; ISO/IEC 42001 (Resources A.4.2); NIST AI RMF: MAP 2.1, MANAGE 1.1). risks.description: Exposure of PII/IP via Model Inversion, Membership Inference, or memorization of sensitive training data.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Apply data minimization, access control, masking, prompt/output safeguards, inference-risk review, logging, and privacy/security testing for AI systems handling sensitive or confidential data.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Prevent unauthorized disclosure, leakage, or inference of sensitive information through AI systems.

risks.description: Failure to rigorously test AI models for accuracy, robustness, bias, and security prior to deployment, leading to performance failures.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Define and execute independent validation before release, including acceptance criteria, test data, performance, robustness, bias, security, limitations, and approval evidence.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Confirm AI systems meet intended requirements and risk tolerances before operational reliance.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (ISO/IEC 5338 (Verification); ISO/IEC 42001 (Control A.6.2.4); MITRE: Test & Evaluation; NIST AI RMF: MEASURE 1.1, MEASURE 2.6). risks.name: Prompt Injection & Input Manipulation
risks.description: Crafting adversarial inputs to manipulate model behavior, bypass filters, or execute unauthorized actions.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Test and mitigate prompt injection and malicious input scenarios using input validation, instruction hierarchy, retrieval/tool isolation, output constraints, monitoring, and user education.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Reduce the likelihood that hostile inputs override AI instructions, expose data, or trigger unauthorized actions.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (OWASP LLM Top 10: LLM01; OWASP ML Top 10: ML01; Gartner: AI Governance; NIST AI RMF: MANAGE 2.5, MEASURE 2.6). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Ineffective Use Case Prioritization
risks.description: The process for selecting AI projects does not align with strategic goals, value potential, or feasibility (e.g., failing to distinguish between "Defend," "Extend," and "Upend").
risks.expectedControlName: AI use-case prioritization and intake control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Apply a documented intake and prioritization process that scores AI use cases for strategic value, feasibility, risk, data readiness, control needs, and expected benefits before funding or build approval.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Direct resources to AI use cases with justified value, feasible delivery, and proportionate control coverage.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Value; Gartner: AI Roadmap; MITRE: Strategy; NIST AI RMF: MAP 1.3, MAP 1.4). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Value Elusiveness
risks.description: Inability to measure tangible benefits due to a lack of clear metrics, productivity leaks, or failure to reinvest time saved.
risks.expectedControlName: AI benefits baseline and value-tracking control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require approved value hypotheses, baseline metrics, benefit owners, measurement cadence, and post-implementation benefit review for material AI initiatives.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Verify whether AI investments create measurable value and enable corrective action where benefits are not realized.

risks.name: Uncontrolled Operational Costs (DoS)
risks.description: Excessive costs from AI services (API calls, compute) or malicious Model Denial of Service attacks causing resource exhaustion.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Monitor model, compute, token, storage, and integration usage against budgets and anomaly thresholds, with rate limits, alerts, and approval gates for material cost increases.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Prevent uncontrolled AI operating cost growth and cost-amplification abuse.

risks.name: Pseudoscience / Scientific Invalidity
risks.description: The AI is tasked with predicting something that cannot scientifically be predicted (e.g., physiognomy, predicting criminality from facial features), leading to fundamentally invalid results.
risks.expectedControlName: Scientific validity and evidence challenge control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require documented scientific rationale, method validation, limitations, peer or expert challenge, and evidence review before relying on AI outputs for scientific or technical claims.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure AI-supported claims and decisions rest on valid methods and evidence rather than unsupported or pseudoscientific reasoning.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (NIST AI RMF: MEASURE 2.2 (Validity), MAP 1.2 (Scientific Integrity); Princeton AI Snake Oil). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Organizational Readiness Gap
risks.description: The rapid evolution of AI capabilities outpaces the organization's ability to adopt them due to siloed structures or lack of cross-functional collaboration.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Assess governance, people, process, data, technology, legal, security, and support readiness before scaling material AI use cases, with gaps tracked to accountable owners.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Confirm the organization can operate and control AI safely before adoption or scale-up.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Roadmap; Gartner: AI Strategy; MITRE: Organization; NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 1.2, GOVERN 2.2). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Lack of Specialized AI Talent
risks.description: The inability to hire, develop, or retain talent with necessary niche technical skills (e.g., data scientists, prompt engineers) hinders strategy execution.
risks.expectedControlName: AI specialist capability and escalation model
risks.expectedControlDescription: Maintain an AI capability model identifying required specialist roles, minimum qualifications, external support triggers, and escalation paths for high-risk AI assurance topics.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure AI work and assurance are supported by people with appropriate technical, risk, and domain expertise.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Organization; Gartner: AI Engineering (Skills); NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 2.2). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Skills & Literacy Gap
risks.description: Insufficient AI literacy across the general workforce prevents effective adoption, leads to poor decision-making, or results in accidental misuse.
risks.expectedControlName: AI literacy and role-based training control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Provide role-based AI literacy, risk, policy, and escalation training for users, owners, developers, risk managers, and auditors, with completion tracked and refreshed periodically.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure personnel understand AI limitations, responsibilities, and control expectations relevant to their role.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Literacy Roadmap; ISO/IEC 42001 (Competence 7.2); MITRE: Workforce; NIST AI RMF: GOVERN 2.2). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Overreliance & Loss of Agency
risks.description: Users accepting AI results without verification or delegating too much control, leading to loss of human agency or Anthropomorphism.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Define where human review is required, what independent evidence must be checked, how exceptions are escalated, and how overreliance indicators are monitored.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Preserve meaningful human judgement and prevent blind acceptance of AI outputs.

risks.expectedControlDescription: Establish and periodically review an AI governance framework covering policy, roles, risk appetite, lifecycle controls, inventory, classification, monitoring, incidents, and reporting.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Provide a coherent management system for governing AI risks across the organization.

risks.name: Unmanaged AI Acquisition & Use
risks.description: Business units acquiring, enabling, or using AI tools and services outside approved governance, security, procurement, or architecture processes, creating unmanaged data, control, and contractual risks.
risks.expectedControlName: AI acquisition and shadow-use approval control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require approval, risk review, security/privacy assessment, and inventory registration before acquiring, building, or materially using AI tools, including third-party and end-user tools.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Prevent unmanaged AI adoption and ensure AI use enters the control framework before material reliance.

risks.name: Contextual Data Failure
risks.description: Using data that is technically accurate but essentially "wrong" for the specific AI use case or context, leading to misleading outputs.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Evaluate whether data used by AI is fit for the intended context, including relevance, completeness, representativeness, timeliness, limitations, and approved use constraints.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Ensure AI outputs are based on data appropriate to the business context and decision.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Data Guide; ISO/IEC 5338; MITRE: Data; NIST AI RMF: MAP 2.3, MEASURE 2.2). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Metadata & Lineage Management Failure
risks.description: Failure to manage technical metadata, lineage, and data/model documentation as operational infrastructure, weakening traceability, reproducibility, explainability, and internal governance over data and model dependencies.
risks.expectedControlDescription: Capture and maintain data origin, transformations, ownership, quality checks, access history, and lineage for datasets used in material AI systems.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Make AI data traceable, explainable, and auditable across collection, preparation, use, and change.

risks.name: Model Drift & Decay
risks.description: The degradation of model performance over time as real-world data diverges from training data (Data/Concept Drift).
risks.expectedControlDescription: Monitor model input, output, performance, data distribution, and business-context drift against thresholds, with documented triggers for investigation, recalibration, rollback, or retirement.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Detect and respond to degradation in AI performance or relevance during operation.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Engineering; MITRE: Solution Monitoring; OWASP ML Top 10: ML08; NIST AI RMF: MANAGE 4.2, MEASURE 2.12). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.

risks.name: Hallucinations (Confabulation)
risks.description: The model produces factually incorrect results that users accept as truth, compromising decision-making and eroding trust.
risks.expectedControlName: AI output accuracy and grounding control
risks.expectedControlDescription: Require grounding, source citation where feasible, confidence/limitation disclosure, human review for material outputs, and testing of hallucination-prone workflows.
risks.expectedControlObjective: Reduce reliance on fabricated, inaccurate, or unsupported AI outputs.
risks.controlSourceBasis: Source-grounded: derived from the row references (Gartner: AI Governance; MITRE: Robust & Reliable; MIT AI Risk Rep: 3.1; NIST AI RMF: MEASURE 2.3). Control wording is an Internal Audit interpretation of the cited source families, not verbatim source text.
